title: Overview of program statements and operations

sentences.text: The fundamental program elements of test cases, functions and altsteps are expressions, basic program statements such as assignments, loop constructs, etc. behavioural statements such as sequential behaviour, alternative behaviour, interleaving, defaults, etc. and operations such as send, receive, create, etc.
Statements can be either single statements (which do not include other program statements) or compound statements (which may include other statements and statement blocks).
Statements shall be executed in the order of their appearance, i.e. sequentially, as illustrated in figure 8.
**Figure 8: Illustration of sequential behaviour**
The individual statements in the sequence shall be separated by the delimiter ";".
EXAMPLE:
MyPort.send(Mymessage); MyTimer.start; log("Done!");
The specification of an empty statement block, i.e. {}, may be found in compound statements, e.g. a branch in an alt statement, and implies that no actions are taken.
Table 16 gives an overview of the TTCN-3 expressions, statements and operations and restrictions on their usage.
Table 16: Overview of TTCN-3 expressions, statements and operations

requirements.subject: ent:testcase
requirements.canonical: The program elements of a testcase, a function and an altstep ARE expressions, basic program statements, behavioural statements and operations.
requirements.original: The fundamental program elements of test cases, functions and altsteps are expressions, basic program statements such as assignments, loop constructs, etc. behavioural statements such as sequential behaviour, alternative behaviour, interleaving, defaults, etc. and operations such as send, receive, create, etc.

ambiguity.issue: 'test cases' is used for the TTCN-3 language element; the keyword-based term is 'testcase'.

requirements.subject: ent:statement
requirements.canonical: A statement IS either a single statement or a compound statement.
requirements.original: Statements can be either single statements (which do not include other program statements) or compound statements (which may include other statements and statement blocks).

requirements.subject: ent:single-statement
requirements.canonical: A single statement IS NOT allowed to include other program statements.
requirements.original: Statements can be either single statements (which do not include other program statements) or compound statements (which may include other statements and statement blocks).

requirements.subject: ent:compound-statement
requirements.canonical: A compound statement MAY include other statements and statement blocks.
requirements.original: Statements can be either single statements (which do not include other program statements) or compound statements (which may include other statements and statement blocks).

requirements.subject: ent:statement
requirements.canonical: Statements SHALL be executed sequentially in the order of their appearance.
requirements.original: Statements shall be executed in the order of their appearance, i.e. sequentially, as illustrated in figure 8.

requirements.subject: ent:statement
requirements.canonical: Statements in a sequence SHALL be separated by the delimiter ";".
requirements.original: The individual statements in the sequence shall be separated by the delimiter ";".

requirements.subject: ent:empty-statement-block
requirements.canonical: An empty statement block `{}` MAY be used in a compound statement, e.g. as a branch of an `alt` statement.
requirements.original: The specification of an empty statement block, i.e. {}, may be found in compound statements, e.g. a branch in an alt statement, and implies that no actions are taken.

requirements.subject: ent:empty-statement-block
requirements.canonical: Execution of an empty statement block `{}` IS without any action.
requirements.original: The specification of an empty statement block, i.e. {}, may be found in compound statements, e.g. a branch in an alt statement, and implies that no actions are taken.
